paper.title_en: Optical Magnus effect on gravitational lensing
paper.abstract_en: The optical Magnus effect refers to a transverse shift of a trajectory of light caused by its polarization and arises as a correction to geometrical optics at the linear order in wavelength. Here, we start from Maxwell's equations in a curved spacetime to derive the equations of motion for a wave packet of circularly polarized light, which confirm the known results involving the helicity-dependent anomalous velocity with some generalization and clarification. We then study possible consequences of the optical Magnus effect on gravitational lensing in the Schwarzschild spacetime as well as in an expanding spacetime with a weak gravitational potential. Among others, by formulating a lens equation modified to incorporate the optical Magnus effect, the Einstein ring is found impossible to emerge from a point source for any axially symmetric thin lens. Analytic solutions to the modified lens equation are also obtained for simple lens models, illuminating how image formation is affected by the optical Magnus effect.
